risks.risk: Commodity risk on raw-material availability and pricing
risks.note: Pelagic fish availability and pricing are subject to seasonal patterns, fishing bans and El Niño-linked events, which the Company flags as a direct risk to its core marine-ingredient business; management separately notes that lower anchovy quotas in Peru and Chile and El Niño concerns tightened fishmeal and fish-oil supplies.

The Company discloses that current borrowings exceeded total equity at FY26-end, and that CARE Ratings downgraded it to BBB-/A3 with a negative outlook; management states it remains focused on deleveraging and working-capital discipline.
Flagged given the high export revenue share — exports contributed approximately 79.7% of FY26 revenue across 25+ countries, so realisations and margins are exposed to currency movement.

risks.risk: Regulatory and trade-policy risk across export jurisdictions
risks.note: The Company operates across multiple export markets and flags regulatory/trade-policy risk; the cautionary statement lists regulatory changes among factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.

risks.risk: Execution risk on new projects and geographies
risks.note: Explicitly flagged on the Oman facility, the Sri Lanka entry and the Bengaluru waste-management ramp-up — all newly announced or under development, so returns depend on commissioning and ramp-up going to plan.

risks.risk: Concentration risk in the newer verticals
risks.note: The newer verticals are reliant on a limited number of large contracts at this stage, so the waste-management and environmental-solutions revenue base depends heavily on individual awards such as the Bengaluru legacy-leachate contract.

risks.risk: Climate and sustainability risk to raw-material availability
risks.note: Flagged across the value chain; management also notes that climate-related events such as El Niño may create both opportunities and challenges for the marine-ingredients industry.

The cautionary statement identifies global and domestic economic conditions, raw-material availability and prices, and climatic and geopolitical developments as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially; the MD message also cites geopolitical uncertainties, supply-chain disruptions and commodity volatility during the year.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mukka Proteins Limited is one of India's prominent manufacturers and exporters of fish protein and animal protein and one of the country's largest producers of fishmeal, fish oil and fish soluble paste, holding an estimated 25%-30% share of India's fishmeal and fish oil segment by revenue.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and supplies Fish Protein products comprising Fish Meal, Fish Oil and Fish Soluble Paste, which are key ingredients in aqua feed (for fish and shrimp), poultry feed (for broiler and layer) and pet food (dog and cat food); fish oil also finds application in pharmaceutical products including Omega-3 supplements, as well as in soap manufacturing, leather tanneries and paint industries. It has evolved from a single-product fishmeal producer into an integrated, multi-vertical platform spanning Fish Protein, Alternate (Insect) Protein, Waste Management & Environmental Solutions, and Frozen & Value-Added Marine Products. It caters to both domestic and international markets, exporting to over 25 countries from manufacturing and blending facilities across coastal India (Karnataka, Gujarat) and the Middle East (Oman).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fish Protein:** Fish meal (60%-65% protein content), Fish oil (rich in Omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA), Fish soluble paste
- **Alternate (Insect) Protein:** Insect meal, Insect oil, Insect compost, Humic acid, Briquettes
- **Waste Management & Environmental Solutions:** Leachate management solutions, Black Soldier Fly municipal wet-waste processing
- **Frozen & Value-Added Marine Products:** Surimi, Crustaceans, Cephalopods, Scombroid/Non-Scombroid fish products

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Aquaculture feed (fish and shrimp) — approximately 91% of fishmeal use
- Poultry feed (broiler and layer)
- Pet food (dog and cat food)
- Swine feed
- Omega-3 nutraceutical and pharmaceutical supplements
- Industrial applications — soap manufacturing, leather tanneries and paint industries
- Municipal bodies (waste-management vertical)
- Exports to over 25 countries including Bahrain, Bangladesh, Chile, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, China, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Oman, Taiwan and Vietnam; exports were approximately 79.7% of FY26 revenue

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global marine-ingredient supply squeeze — repeated curtailment of Peru's North-Central anchovy season amid coastal El Niño conditions, with cumulative global fishmeal production down 26-28% year-on-year through Q1 CY2026 — has been directly supportive of realisations for producers with diversified sourcing and processing scale, and has visibly benefited the Company's pricing and margin trajectory through FY26
- Lower anchovy quotas in Peru and Chile and El Niño concerns tightened fishmeal and fish-oil supplies, raising international prices and reinforcing the importance of reliable sourcing and diversified protein solutions
- Feed-grade aquatic-animal demand is forecast to grow faster than food-use demand (+5.8% to 17.4 MMT in 2025 versus +1.6% for direct human consumption), consistent with continued fishmeal/fish-oil tightness
- Aquaculture now supplies essentially all incremental growth in global seafood supply, with FAO projecting total aquatic-animal supply of about 214 MMT by 2034 — a structural demand base for feed ingredients
- Rabobank flags that the continuing shift toward carnivorous, premium finfish species will increase demand for fishmeal even as supply growth stays constrained
- Insect protein, and Black Soldier Fly protein in particular, is emerging as a credible ESG-aligned substitute for conventional fishmeal precisely as the fishmeal supply environment tightens, with broadening regulatory support globally
- Policy tailwind in India: the Union Government reduced import duty on fishmeal and vitamin premixes from 15% to 5% and on fish oil and algal premix from 30% to 15%, lowering input costs across the aquafeed chain, while the RoDTEP scheme continued to support exporter margins
- US tariff recalibration reduced the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from a peak of 50% to approximately 18%, with further product-specific relief for seafood — supportive of the frozen and value-added seafood export vertical
- Legacy-dumpsite remediation and scientific leachate treatment remain structurally under-penetrated, with high entry barriers (technology, regulatory approval, execution track record) that favour early, credible movers
- Better realizations, an improved product mix and disciplined execution drove Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expansion of 421 bps to 12.9%
- Operational expansion initiatives undertaken during the year are expected to contribute to improved operational efficiencies, higher throughput and greater revenue visibility
- ₹474.89 crore contract awarded by Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited for the scientific treatment and disposal of legacy leachate, described as a significant milestone for the Leachate Management & Environmental Solutions vertical and a platform for pursuing future waste-management and resource-recovery opportunities
- Management states that operational expansion initiatives are expected to support greater revenue visibility

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build a diversified, future-ready enterprise on four growth pillars — Fish Protein, Alternate Protein, Waste Management & Environmental Solutions, and Frozen & Value-Added Marine Products
- Diversify beyond traditional marine protein: entry into the Waste Management segment through Leachate Management solutions and into Frozen & Value-Added Products (Surimi, Crustaceans, Cephalopods and Scombroid/Non-Scombroid products), broadening presence across the marine, environmental and food-processing value chain
- Scale the Black Soldier Fly alternate-protein platform that converts organic/municipal wet waste into insect meal, insect oil and compost on a zero-landfill, zero-leachate, circular-economy basis
- Monetise sustainability: build the carbon-credit portfolio through the Bengaluru BSF wet-waste project listed on the Verra Registry (Project ID 5893), progressing towards Verified Carbon Unit issuance
- Expand the international footprint — develop the Oman manufacturing facility at Aljoubah Industrial Area to strengthen raw-material access and export-market presence, and enter Sri Lanka through the incorporation of Lanka Bio Proteins Private Limited
- Grow through acquisition and consolidation of group entities — completed acquisition of Ento Proteins Private Limited and of the remaining stake in Haris Marine Products Private Limited, with further stake acquisitions in Delta Marine Products and Aqua Marine approved
- Strengthen responsible sourcing and traceability through alignment with the MarinTrust Improver Programme, to reduce sourcing risk and support compliance with global standards in international markets
- Alongside growth, focus on cost optimization, deleveraging, working-capital discipline and prudent capital allocation

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As at end-FY26 the Group operated 25 manufacturing units (including third-party/job-work units), of which 17 are owned, in-house facilities across India and Oman. The principal expansion under way is a new international facility in the Aljoubah Industrial Area, Oman, spread over 21,249 sq. mt, expected to add approximately 400 TPD of fish meal, fish oil and paste capacity and to commence operations over the coming quarters, strengthening Middle East presence and raw-material access. In the environmental vertical, the Company secured a ₹474.89 crore (ex-GST) contract from Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited for scientific treatment and disposal of legacy leachate at the Mittaganahalli and Kannur sites — a first-of-its-kind project at this scale involving approximately ₹100 crore of capex, an approximately six-month build period and a four-year project term. The Black Soldier Fly wet-waste platform carries an approved waste-management input capacity of 1,400 tonnes per day across Mangaluru (200 TPD), Bengaluru (1,000 TPD) and Kochi (200 TPD); separately, FY26 incremental carbon-credit-eligible capacity approvals took the total to 1,200 TPD (EPPL 200 TPD + MPL 300 TPD + an incremental 700 TPD approved), with the project listed on Verra Registry 3 advancing the pathway to carbon-credit issuance. Corporate expansion during FY26 comprised the acquisition of Ento Proteins Private Limited into a wholly owned subsidiary (consideration ₹32.30 lakh, completed February 24, 2026), acquisition of the remaining 2% of Haris Marine Products Private Limited for ₹19.64 lakh, the renaming of a subsidiary to MPL HRC Jathin Ecosolutions LLP (March 17, 2026) to house the Bengaluru waste-management and legacy-leachate joint venture (76% MPL stake), board approval for incorporation of and up to ₹2.50 crore investment in Lanka Bio Proteins Private Limited in Sri Lanka (49% stake) — the Company's first step into Sri Lanka — and continued consolidation across Ocean Proteins Private Limited, GSM Marine Export, Mukka Frozen Impex and United Gulf Fishery Products LLC (Oman). Quality infrastructure supporting the footprint includes steam-sterilised, mechanised fishmeal plants and a dedicated blending unit and quality-assurance laboratory in Gujarat.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Estimated 25%-30% share of India's fishmeal and fish oil segment by revenue and of Indian fish-protein exports
- Five-decade operating history tracing back to the founding of the Mukka Group in 1977, evolving from a single-product fishmeal producer to a multi-vertical platform
- Export presence across 25+ countries with export revenue approximately 79.7% of FY26 revenue, supported by an integrated sourcing and manufacturing network
- Long-standing global customer relationships and custom/application-specific formulation capability in the fish-protein segment
- Steam-sterilised, mechanised fishmeal plants plus a dedicated blending unit and quality-assurance laboratory, with GMP+, HACCP and ISO certifications, Export Inspection Council registration and a China-registered export licence
- Positioned as one of the pioneers of large-scale Black Soldier Fly insect-protein production co-located with municipal solid waste processing in India, giving an early-mover position in a high-entry-barrier vertical
- Manufacturing and raw-material access across both coastal India and the Middle East (Oman), diversifying sourcing

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Commodity risk on raw-material availability and pricing — Pelagic fish availability and pricing are subject to seasonal patterns, fishing bans and El Niño-linked events, which the Company flags as a direct risk to its core marine-ingredient business; management separately notes that lower anchovy quotas in Peru and Chile and El Niño concerns tightened fishmeal and fish-oil supplies.
- Leverage risk and credit-rating downgrade — The Company discloses that current borrowings exceeded total equity at FY26-end, and that CARE Ratings downgraded it to BBB-/A3 with a negative outlook; management states it remains focused on deleveraging and working-capital discipline.
- Foreign exchange risk — Flagged given the high export revenue share — exports contributed approximately 79.7% of FY26 revenue across 25+ countries, so realisations and margins are exposed to currency movement.
- Regulatory and trade-policy risk across export jurisdictions — The Company operates across multiple export markets and flags regulatory/trade-policy risk; the cautionary statement lists regulatory changes among factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- Execution risk on new projects and geographies — Explicitly flagged on the Oman facility, the Sri Lanka entry and the Bengaluru waste-management ramp-up — all newly announced or under development, so returns depend on commissioning and ramp-up going to plan.
- Concentration risk in the newer verticals — The newer verticals are reliant on a limited number of large contracts at this stage, so the waste-management and environmental-solutions revenue base depends heavily on individual awards such as the Bengaluru legacy-leachate contract.
- Climate and sustainability risk to raw-material availability — Flagged across the value chain; management also notes that climate-related events such as El Niño may create both opportunities and challenges for the marine-ingredients industry.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical exposure — The cautionary statement identifies global and domestic economic conditions, raw-material availability and prices, and climatic and geopolitical developments as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially; the MD message also cites geopolitical uncertainties, supply-chain disruptions and commodity volatility during the year.
